findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There was a live mouse observed on the shelves of the outdoor storage shed. There wasn't any food observed within the unit, however, there are single service items and other miscellaneous items that’s related to the facility. Mouse droppings were also observed on the shelves and floor of the storage shed. The PIC discussed having the shed cleaned, as well as seal holes that might act as an entry point for rodents. Will follow up on July 24, 2026 to ensure that there is no sign of rodent activity.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee operate faucet handles with bare hands after the handwashing process. Discussed with PIC proper handwashing procedures. Ensure that employees are using barriers to turn off faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The sanitizer bucket in the bar area tested at 0ppm (quat). The PIC mentioned that the sani bucket was mistakenly filled with plain water. Quaternary ammonia was added to the solution and was tested at 400ppm to correct the violation.

There was one sanitizer bucket on the cook-line that tested to be at 0ppm of Quaternary ammonium and one sanitizer bucket in the back preparation area that tested to be at 100ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Both sanitizer buckets were remade and tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. 

Ensure that all sanitizer buckets are testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The fan guards of the walk in cooler were observed accumulated with dust. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.comment: A personal drink cup was stored on a shelf directly above clean dishes along the dish table of the dish machine. Discussed and shown to PIC. The drink cup was discarded. Be sure to educate employees on proper drink storage. Ensure that personal drinks are never stored above clean dishes to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There were several ceiling tiles that were out of place in many areas of the kitchen. These areas include, but aren’t limited to, the dry storage closet (over single service items & food), in the dish room (over clean dishes), and in the back storage room (over clean utensils). Discussed and shown to PIC. The facility mentioned that the ceiling tiles were popped out of place to allow heat to travel to the pipes to prevent them from freezing during harsh temperatures. The ceiling tiles were put back in place during the inspection to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed holes in the ceiling above the ice machines to not be sealed. The holes are suspected to be the entry points for the raccoons that have been spotted throughout the facility. Discussed with PIC. Will follow-up 10/21/2024 to ensure holes have been sealed and that there aren’t any raccoons present in the facility. 

6-202.16: Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed at least two employees wash hands and not use a barrier to operate faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed with PIC. Be sure to educate employees to always use a barrier when turning off faucet handles to prevent recontaminating hands after washing them. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed a scoop stored in the flour bin with the handle directly touching the flour. Discussed with PIC and the scoop was taken to the back to be rewashed and re-sanitized. Ensure that the flour scoop is stored in a manner that prevents contamination.  

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed a clean plate with food residue on it to be stored in the plate cooler. PIC removed the plate from the cooler. Ensure that food contact surfaces that have been cleaned are free of debris during storage. 

4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed thawing meat to not be completely submerged under running water. PIC transferred the meat to a larger container and also turned on the faucet to allow water to run. Ensure that thawing meats are completely submerged in running water at all times. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: The tongs being stored to obtain the breadsticks by the waitstaff are observed to be hanging on the holder on the front of the counter. These tongs were being pressed against by the front of the uniform of each employee observed to be getting breadsticks. The contaminated tongs were removed and placed in the dish area for the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle and clean tongs were placed in this area on the counter to prevent waitstaff from contaminating the food contact surface of the tongs. PIC is going to change practices on how to store the tongs to prevent contamination of the tongs food contact surface. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Dish machine temperature test strips are on order and should arrive as of 9/26/23. Temperature test strips originally ordered were 180F strips, and 160F strips are needed. The correct strips were ordered and will be available for use this week.
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Functioning eyewash station is present on the faucet of the handwashing sink across from dry storage room in the back prep area. Removal of the eyewash station was discussed during the 4/17/23 routine inspection and documented in the general comments of that report noting it was to be removed by the next routine inspection. Handwashing sinks are to be used for handwashing only, and the eyewash station needs to be removed. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. 

POST INSPECTION NOTE: Manager on duty sent a photo via text after inspector left the facility to show eyewash station, which was screwed on to the faucet, was removed. Photo will be attached to report once uploaded in reporting system.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solutions in prep area sani-buckets were observed at concentrations of 100ppm and lower. Full jug of quat product was connected to the dispenser. Sani-buckets were refreshed with solutions at proper concentration of 200ppm.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration. Also, consider pre-soaking wiping cloths with sanitizer prior to storage in a fresh solution to help minimize absorption of chemical out of solution into wiping cloths.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Half gallons of milk and half and half were observed without date marks in the bar and server area coolers. Products without dates were discarded. Other half gallons were observed with day dots. Make sure all staff consistently provide date marks for open half gallons of dairy products.
A Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Dish machine temperature test strips could not be found during inspection. Manger messaged GM and test strips were ordered during the inspection. Test strips should arrive by the next operating day. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16)  Priority violations were observed for sanitization and cold holding. Quat solution was dispensing at 0ppm due to the absence of product. An unopened, fresh jug was sitting next to the empty jug still connected to the dispenser. PIC immediately corrected the issue and replaced the product to allow for proper dispensing of quat solutions at 200ppm. GM noted the technician was out recently to recalibrate the machine, and it was believed the staff allowed the dispenser to run nonstop causing unexpected/excessive use of product. Regardless of the reason, all staff need to be trained to know and understand the basic function of the chemical dispenser as well as basic troubleshooting. Staff should also be trained to let management know when product is empty/needs to be replaced and/or if other issues occur.
Portions of spinach and kale were observed with surface temperatures above 60F and internal temperatures ranging from 46F to 54F in pans held in an ice bath in the server alley. Corrective actions were taken and options for storage and best practices were discussed (see #22 for details). 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signs were not posted in the restrooms. Handwashing signs were provided and posted during inspection.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handwashing sink in back prep area was used to fill bucket with hot water. Employee was advised on proper use of handwashing sink for handwashing only. Management was advised to revisit proper use of handwashing sinks with all staff. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-buckets were observed at concentrations of 100ppm for solutions prepared earlier in the day and 0ppm for solutions that were just prepared. The sanitizer jug at the dispenser was empty and observed with a jug of full, unopened product next to it. PIC replaced the sanitizer, and fresh solutions were observed at 200ppm. 
Sani-bucket at bar was also observed at 100ppm during inspection and was refreshed with new solution at 200ppm. Ensure sanitizer solutions are changed throughout the day as needed. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Portions of spinach and kale added to pans of soup were observed with surface temperatures above 60F and internal temperatures ranging from 46F to 54F in pans held in an ice bath in the server alley. GM stated practice will change to allow for majority of product to be cold held in a cooler with only minimum portions in storage area where soup prep occurs. Horizontal instead of vertical storage will also occur to allow for all product to be down inside the pan within the ice bath to allow for optimum cold holding.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.
Cease the practice of storing TCS foods outside of pans in the top holding area of the prep cooler. TC

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11 Employee was observed rolling silverware and having bare hand contact with food contact surfaces of forks due to positioning of utensils with food contact surface extended up out of storage container. Employee was advised on glove use in addition to handwashing when rolling silverware if hand contact with food contact surface is unavoidable. Employee put on gloves to finish rolling silverware.
Sanitized utensils shall be handled so that contamination of food- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11 (A) Utensils at silverware wrapping station were observed to be damp. Ensure proper air drying of utensils prior to rolling silverware. 
After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining as specified in the first paragraph of 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (food-contact surface santizing solutions), before contact with food.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 Drain line to the left ice machine bin was broken and allowing for water to drip and accumulate on the floor beneath. Drain line to the right ice machine bin was pushed back against the wall and not draining in the floor drain. Provide repairs and properly position ice bin drain lines and condensate lines to allow for proper drainage in the floor drain under the ice machines. 
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Floor tiles in dish area were observed damaged and loose with moisture accumulation under some. Majority of damaged tiles were adjacent to the trough drain under the clean dish drain board.
Ponding, murky water was also observed where flooring was damaged and missing around the floor drain under the dirty dish storage counter. 
PIC noted work order has been placed for floor tiles. Ensure all areas of damaged tile and disrepair are addressed.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 DRY STORAGE - Floor under shelving was soiled with general debris, powder, and food debris. 
DISH AREA - 1) General grimy buildup and food splash were observed on the walls, attached plumbing, and undersides of counters. 
2) General surfaces under/around dish machine were soiled with with general buildup of splash/debris.
Clean the floors, walls, and attached plumbing in the aforementioned areas. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed quaternary ammonium concentrations in multiple sani buckets and the bar 3 part sink to be 0ppm-100ppm. Quat concentrations must be maintained at 200ppm-400ppm. Sanitizer concentrations were remade during the inspection. Sanitizer concentrations will be maintained longer if wiping cloths are soaked in sanitizer prior to being placed in a new solution. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed three half gallons of milk that had a manufacturer’s date of 6-5-22. Date marking may not exceed manufacturer dates. The milk was discarded during the inspection. 

3-501.17: (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. Mop was moved to a position that allowed it to air dry. Reference 6-501.16.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizer at the three part sink in the bar area was observed at less than 50 ppm. Chlorine sanitizers used for submersion type sanitizing should be at a minimum of 50 ppm. The sink was remade to correct concentration during the inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) (C) 1) Walls were observed soiled in both server areas below the ice scoops. 2) The floor in the bar area has an section at the end that is accumulating water and debris. 3) The server area on the south side has an accumulation of black mold on the bottom of the ice scoop holder. Inspector instructed the PIC to clean the walls, floors and attached fixtures often enough so as to prevent the accumulation of soilage.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
1) Observed the ice bin in the waitress station to be in the open position when not in use. Keep ice bin closed when not in use. 2) Observed the tea bags to be stored in an open bowl above the tea maker in the waitress station. Store tea bags covered and protected from potential contamination.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
REPEAT> 1) Observed the lid to the ice machine on the left to be cracked on the lip of the lid. Replace or caulk lid so that it is smooth and easily cleanable. 2) Observed a gap in the hood baffles on the left side of the rear hood. Fix gap in hood system. A part was ordered and is the wrong size so a replacement part has been ordered. NEW> 3) Observed the shelves in the salad prep cooler to be rusty. This unit is to be replaced in the next month. 4) Observed the shelf to the left when you walk in the walk in cooler to be rusting. Replace shelves.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
1) Observed a sanitizer bucket on the cook line to test at 0 ppm quat. Provide sanitizer buckets to be 200-400 ppm quat. 2) Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on the prep table in the bread station. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) REPEAT> Observed the undersides of the tables in the dish room to have limescale/food splash build up. NEW> 2) Observed the rack for the glasses in the dish room to be soiled. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor in the dry storage room to be soiled with water and dirt. It appeared that the pipe from the walk in freezer condensation had been misplaced from the floor drain and was collecting on the floors in this area. Clean the floors. 2) Observed the floor drain and the floors along the back wall in the bar area to be heavily soiled. Clean the floors and floor drain.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the wall behind the dish machine to be soiled and moldy. Clean the wall.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
